A1.justification: Despite the changed title, the authors, IIMM definition, and core experiments identify the same work. Both complete PDFs, including their appendices, contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, in-domain gains, out-of-domain forgetting, transferability comparisons, and appendix analyses of embedding measures.

after.justification: v2 retains original fine-tuning results and reports additional baseline comparisons, per-dataset outcomes, and component-weighting and substitution analyses.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 and v2 Equations (2)-(4) define the same equal-weight average of incorrect image-text similarity and pairwise image similarity. Alternative weights and component substitutions are evaluated as ablations; the proposed IIMM procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The original nine classification benchmarks are retained. v2 Tables 5-6 additionally report STL10 results across base models and PEFT methods, expanding reported image-classification coverage. However, the experimental description still lists nine datasets, leaving STL10's inclusion in the aggregate analyses unclear.

E2.justification: v2 adds GBC and H-Score to the retained TransRate, SFDA, NCTI, and EMMS comparisons in Tables 1-2. GBC becomes a leading competitor and receives a separate predictive-fit comparison in Table 3, substantially strengthening the comparison set.

E3.justification: The main ranking evaluations switch from Spearman correlation to Kendall's tau. New analyses fit GBC against log-transformed normalized gains and sweep component weights from 0 to 1. The stated model backbones, validation splits, 30-epoch training budget, batch size, and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged; the linear-probe evaluation is dropped.

E4.justification: v2 Tables 7-8 test sensitivity to inter/intra weighting, and Table 9 substitutes H-Score, TransRate, and GBC for the intra-image component. Most clustering, entropy, and modality-gap screening analyses from v1 Appendix A are removed. The original three-component fit analysis is retained as v2 Table 4.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 7-8 introduce 95% confidence intervals for Pearson correlations in the weighting analysis. Both versions already report p-values and 96% regression confidence bands. No additional experimental repetitions or seed protocol is stated.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline, per-task, weighting, and substitution results while removing clustering/entropy and linear-probe outcomes. In v2 Table 1, GBC ties IIMM for CLIP at tau 0.78 and exceeds it for SigLIP, 0.83 versus 0.78. The original core IIMM regression plots and component fits are retained; changed main-table coefficients use different correlation metrics and do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 1 and its supplementary proof, bounding IIMM changes by delta_A/2 + delta_B under unit-norm assumptions, with an additional finite-sample concentration bound. v1 contains no corresponding theorem or proof. v2 also corrects the stated IIMM range from [0,1] to [-1,1].

C1.justification: v2 adds central claims of a contrastive-learning derivation and theoretically guaranteed stability, and its conclusion claims task-agnostic applicability. v1 primarily contributes empirical prediction of learning and forgetting with geometric intuition. Those empirical claims remain, but the claimed contribution now substantially includes theoretical foundations.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mechanism explanation for CLIP-Adapter's localized representational shifts and qualifies IIMM correlations in relation to near-optimal fine-tuning. It interprets the new bound as supporting stability and acknowledges insufficient power to select an optimal mixing weight. It removes v1's piecewise-threshold hypothesis and explicit caveat about untested applicability beyond vision-language models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and supplementary instructions for computing Kendall's tau. It removes v1's runtime, hardware, software, and memory details, including the 55-minute average training run, approximately 182-hour search, and CUDA version. Core training hyperparameters remain documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on GBC, InfoNCE, transferability surveys, and recent adaptation and generalization work, while removing clustering-index and Welle references. Related work expands the discussion of likelihood-based measures and distinguishes LOVM/SWAB's zero-shot selection from fine-tuning prediction. The central research gap remains the same.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with substantial rewrites of the abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion. Section 3 is reorganized around contrastive-learning principles and a theoretical bound. The earlier appendix structure is replaced by proof, component-weighting, and additional-results sections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column format, replaces the two introductory schematics with a new embedding-geometry diagram, expands comparison tables, and substantially replaces the appendix displays. The original main regression plots reappear as Figures 2-3, with the separate linear-probe panel removed.

improvement.justification: The stronger baseline comparisons, component ablations with uncertainty, and per-task tables improve scrutiny of the empirical argument; the corrected range and stability proof also help. These gains are limited by removed computational details, inconsistent accounting of STL10 within a nine-task protocol, and an overstatement in contribution 3: the theorem's upper bound does not guarantee that large distribution shifts produce large IIMM changes.
